justification: This branch WRITES to served regulatory text in production: 677 provisions across two passes, including setback formulae, wall-height limits and floor-area controls that a planner quotes. Nothing else in the change is close in blast radius, and a wrong transform would corrupt the very numbers the product exists to serve. Critical rather than Standard for that reason alone. It also rewrites the predicate of a live DQ metric twice, and a metric that silently stops seeing its own defect class is how DQ-30 passed while 241 rows stayed broken.

falsifiable_check.command: python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-76; python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-77; python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-78; python scripts/repair_tex_residue.py --pass tex; python scripts/repair_tex_residue.py --pass units
falsifiable_check.fails_when: extraction residue returns to served text, or either repair pass finds rows it can no longer transform within its invariant
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Every number here was watched moving, not asserted. DQ-76 went 10 -> 99 -> 104 as the metric was corrected twice, then 104 -> 9 after the repair. DQ-77 was 581 and is 0. DQ-78 is 111 and stays red. The two metric corrections were themselves observed failures: the first predicate returned CLEAN on 89 rows carrying the identical fault, and the second drove the count to 0 while 103 rows still held braces - both caught by reading data after a green result rather than believing it.

pre_impl.existing_data: regulatory_provisions, served set is_current AND v2_is_actionable = 19,957 rows, unchanged before and after both repair passes. source_council IS NULL for statewide instruments, which is why DQ-27's council-scoped fix could never have reached these rows. A token census of every backslash command actually present (27 distinct macros, all TeX) replaced guessing at the predicate.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Four, and each changed the work. (1) The DQ-76 predicate was a list of macros I had seen, not a description of the fault; it reported clean on 89 of 99 rows. (2) After widening, its brace class could not match an EMPTY '{}' nor '{ : }' nor '{ t h }', so the first repair pass reported success at 0 while 103 rows still carried braces. (3) I assumed the '12 00 { m } 2' rows could be repaired to '1,200 m2'; that joins digits, which is a judgement about the source PDF, so the repair deliberately leaves '12 00 m 2'. (4) I was about to deactivate DQ-78's 111 rows as containing no control. Reading the rows nearest the CUT showed several carry real controls with map text interleaved - deactivating would have hidden binding controls, the liability direction.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: repair_tex_residue.py is a new surface and the prior-art sweep is recorded in its header: repair_shadow_reports.py regenerates satellite report ROWS, cleanup_bad_setbacks.py and delete_bad_leichhardt_rows.py delete from other tables, fix_topics_step1_garbage_cleanup.py rewrites v2_topic not text, and dq_probe_live.py measures this set but is read-only by design and must stay so. The --pass flag follows the shape repair_shadow_reports.py already uses for two authorized passes over one guard chain.
pre_impl.external_source_error: No external source is called. Both repair passes are pure string transforms over text already in regulatory_provisions, and both probes are SELECTs. The relevant failure is therefore the DATABASE being unreachable, not an API: dq_probe_live.run() reports UNKNOWN and exits 2 rather than 0, because 'could not look' must never be read as 'found nothing'. The repair aborts before any write if DATABASE_URL is unset, and rolls the whole transaction back if the connection drops mid-pass.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No frontend type changes. provision_text was and remains a non-null text column, and the repairs only alter its CONTENT. The compliance UI and the report PDFs render it as a string, so a repaired row needs no deploy and no type migration - the corrected text is served on the next read. The visible difference is that a control now reads '3.6 m above ground level' instead of '3.6 { m } above ground level'.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: a planner reading a served control saw markup where the regulated value belongs - a setback formula as '\mathtt { s } = \mathtt { h } - 3 \mathtt { m }', a height limit as '3.6 { m }', a floor area as '12 00 { m } 2'. It fails VISIBLY, which is the one mercy: the reader can tell something is wrong, even though they cannot tell what the number was. The dangerous residue is DQ-78, where scrambled map text sits beside a real control and reads as though it were part of it. After: the text renders as written. The failure mode this change could introduce is a wrong number rendering as a plausible one, which is precisely why each pass asserts an invariant per row and skips rather than writes when it cannot hold.

functions.name: repair
functions.input: a single provision_text string containing TeX math-mode residue such as '\mathfrak { s }' or '{ - }', passed one row at a time from the planning SELECT
functions.output: the same text with TeX wrappers stripped and their contents kept; digits never altered
functions.if_none: without it the 104 rows keep serving markup where a regulated value belongs - '3.6 { m } above ground level' for a height limit

functions.name: repair_units
functions.input: a provision_text whose unit is split across a space
functions.output: the same text with the unit joined: '900 m m' -> '900 mm'. Only spaces are deleted
functions.if_none: 581 rows keep quoting a control as '900 m m' when the instrument says 900mm

functions.name: nonspace
functions.input: any provision_text string, before or after transformation, used to compare the two for the units pass invariant
functions.output: its non-whitespace characters in order - the units pass's invariant
functions.if_none: the units pass would rest on the weaker digit check, which cannot detect a dropped or reordered LETTER

values.read_at: scripts/dq_probe_live.py against production, before and after each pass, 2026-08-15
values.if_missing: the repair would rest on its own UPDATE count, which reports what it did rather than what is left

values.value: 19,957 served rows before and after both passes
values.if_missing: a transform that silently dropped rows would look like a successful repair - the count falling for the wrong reason

values.value: 0 rows skipped by either invariant, across 677 writes
values.read_at: the scripts' own per-row check, printed on both runs
values.if_missing: a skipped row is the signal that a transform is unsafe on some input; zero skips is what makes the blanket application defensible

queries.query: UPDATE regulatory_provisions SET provision_text = %s WHERE id = %s AND provision_text = %s
queries.purpose: Guarded on the text read during planning, so a row changed by another writer between plan and write updates nothing rather than being clobbered. The transaction rolls back if the affected count disagrees with the planned set.
queries.file_line: scripts/repair_tex_residue.py, in main() inside the --apply branch
queries.where_clause: WHERE id = %s AND provision_text = %s - the id targets exactly one row, and the second predicate pins the text read during planning so a row modified by another writer between plan and write matches nothing and is skipped rather than clobbered. The run then rolls back because the affected count disagrees with the planned set.

break_it.scenario: A transform corrupts a regulated number in served provision text.
break_it.what_happens: Cannot reach the database. Each pass asserts an invariant per row before writing - the TeX pass requires the ordered digit sequence to be identical, the units pass the stronger non-whitespace sequence. A row failing is skipped and printed, never written.
break_it.repro: python scripts/repair_tex_residue.py --pass units   # SKIPPED count must be 0
break_it.how: Per-row invariant check in main(), plus a full before/after JSON backup written before any UPDATE and an abort if it cannot be saved.

break_it.scenario: The repair silently diverges from the metric, so the row can never close.
break_it.what_happens: It already happened: a brace class of [-A-Za-z0-9] left 103 rows behind while the metric read 0.
break_it.repro: diff the PREDICATE constant in repair_tex_residue.py against PROBES['DQ-76'] in dq_probe_live.py
break_it.mitigated: Yes - the comment was replaced with a test after this report first recorded it as only a convention.
break_it.how: tests/test_repair_matches_probe.py asserts each repair predicate is CONTAINED in its probe's SQL, so a repair can never touch a row the metric is not watching. Mutation-verified: reintroducing the exact [-A-Za-z0-9] brace class that caused the 103-row miss makes the test fail.

break_it.scenario: Deactivating DQ-78's 111 rows would hide a control that binds a development.
break_it.what_happens: Would have happened. The bulk remedy was planned and abandoned after reading the rows nearest the cut, several of which carry real controls with map text interleaved.
break_it.repro: python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-78 then read ids 95870, 95375, 95887
break_it.how: DQ-78's ledger note and tracker row both record the reversal and why, so the bulk fix is not reached for again.

break_it.scenario: A repair blinds its own metric, hiding a defect it did not fix.
break_it.what_happens: It did. Stripping '$' from '$F o o d A c t 2003' removed the symptom DQ-76 could see and left the letter-spacing corruption invisible.
break_it.repro: python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-77   # the class that was left behind
break_it.how: The surviving class was measured and opened as DQ-77 and DQ-78 rather than quietly folded into DQ-76's predicate, so how it was found stays on the record.

break_it.scenario: A concurrent writer's edit is clobbered part-way through a repair pass.
break_it.what_happens: The guarded UPDATE affects 0 rows, the totals disagree, and the whole transaction rolls back.
break_it.repro: inspect the UPDATE in main(): WHERE id = %s AND provision_text = %s
break_it.how: Per-row guard on the planned text, single transaction, rollback on any count mismatch.

mutation_analysis: The repairs were mutation-tested by construction rather than after the fact: the invariant IS the mutation test, run per row on live data, and it passed 677 times with zero skips. The metrics were tested by perturbation - DQ-76's predicate returns 0 for marrickville against the same signatures, so it discriminates rather than matching everything, and DQ-78's SQL form was cross-checked against an independent Python implementation that scored every served row (both 111). The two rejected DQ-76 signatures are the strongest evidence the metric is not merely permissive: digit-spacing (87 rows) and superscript-brace (8 rows) were measured, found to match '100 Year ARI Flood Level' and markdown ids like 14e_3, and excluded, because a signature that cannot be wrong makes a number that cannot fall.
residual_risk: DQ-76 stays open at 9: each is a LONE brace substituting for a character rather than wrapping one - 7 HTML cells reading '200m{-300m2' where '{' replaced a '2', plus two where a brace replaced a parenthesis. Deciding which character a lone brace should be needs the source document, so they are deliberately not guessed. DQ-78 stays open at 111 with its remedy corrected but not applied - stripping figure text from a provision needs the source PDF's layout, which the extractor discarded. Digit-splitting ('12 00' for 1,200, '4 000' for 4,000) is untouched by both passes and is NOT tracked by any row yet; it is visible in the repaired text and deserves one. Predicate drift is now guarded by a test rather than a comment (tests/test_repair_matches_probe.py), mutation-verified against the exact drift that caused the 103-row miss.

post_merge.db_reset: No. Two UPDATE passes over provision_text only; no schema change, no migration, no row added or removed. Full before/after backups are in .claude/backups/tex_residue_repair_*.json if a revert is ever needed.
post_merge.verify: python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-76 returns 9, --id DQ-77 returns 0, --id DQ-78 returns 111; served row count is 19,957.
post_merge.secrets: None added, read or referenced. Both scripts use the existing DATABASE_URL via dotenv.
post_merge.other_repo: None. All changes are in this repository. No deployed service reads dq_checks.json or the tracker; the repaired text is read by the compliance API from the database, which needs no deploy.
post_merge.manual_verify: Open a served DCP control that was repaired - id 37643 should now read 's = h - 3 m' and id 45614 '3.6 m above ground level' - and confirm the rendered report shows the number rather than markup. Then read two DQ-78 rows near the cut (95870, 95375) and confirm for yourself that they contain real controls, because the decision NOT to deactivate them rests on that.
